scientific_question: Does the incremental value of occupied-source graph topology attenuate again when a species is so widespread across pilot islands that its occupied source pool is close to saturated?

hypothesis.name: broad_occupancy_source_saturation
hypothesis.statement: For species with very few pilot absences, occupied-source topology should add less heldout information beyond R3 than it did in the original 79-species exploratory layer.
hypothesis.primary_future_contrast: equal-block mean[(C-R3)_broad_layer - (C-R3)_original79] across the same 168 heldout blocks
hypothesis.future_support_rule: paired-block contrast point > 0 and paired block-bootstrap 95% lower bound > 0
hypothesis.secondary_future_external_isolation_pred: within the broad layer, block C-minus-R3 is positively associated with response-independent Current_isolation; this secondary cannot rescue a failed primary

broad_layer_rule.reason_zero_absence_excluded: at least one pilot absence is required so the species has both response classes in the pilot
broad_layer_rule.rare96_disjointness: sealed rare layer required pilot presence between 5 and 12
broad_layer_rule.if_fewer_than_minimum: terminal NOT_ESTIMABLE for this broad-end test; do not widen the absence range using heldout outcomes

next_step_if_gate_passes: freeze exact R3/C predictions and a response-independent broad-layer source-saturation diagnostic before opening any broad-layer heldout occurrence
